sentiment.instructions: Judge the overall sentiment of the tweet: the author's own attitude (including implied criticism, sarcasm or excitement), or, for news-style headlines, the clear valence of the reported event. Apply the neutral carve-outs first; they override surface cues like '!', '...', 'free' or 'Nooo'.

criteria.positive:
The author shows enthusiasm, love, praise, gratitude, enjoyment, hope, prayers, RIP condolences, playful encouragement ('get it', ':-)'), or eager personal anticipation ('can't wait', 'this time tomorrow I'll be...!', 'for sure going to', <3). Also:
- Hyped or celebratory calls to action: 'come support', 'come celebrate', free treats, holiday specials, 'get your tickets now!', giveaways.
- Favourable predictions.
- News of big achievements: winning a title, reaching a final, records, milestones.
criteria.neutral:
No real stance, including these carve-outs:
- Dry organizational notices ('register', 'RSVP', meetings, listings, interview links) and fan pleas to celebrities.
- Routine or early-round results and in-progress scores.
- Weather, trivia, questions, polls, and casual plans.
- Speculative or soft news.
- Mild comparative opinions.
- Teasing quips about athletes, teams, films, games or companies.
- Snarky one-line asides on shared news or celebrity or political gaffes ('clear as mud', 'Bwahahaha', 'NEVER!!!').
- Minor personal inconveniences or scheduling clashes told jokingly ('lmao', 'I'm dead', 'not ready', 'Nooo', 'sorry for...').
criteria.negative:
Includes:
- Genuine disappointment, sadness, frustration, boredom, dread or missing out ('sucks', 'disappointed', 'going to die', ':(').
- Serious criticism, disapproval, skepticism or sarcasm about policies, politicians' conduct, violence, ethics, insensitivity, products or people, even when phrased calmly or as a rhetorical question ('was he really...?', '#justsaying').
- Headlines reporting clearly bad events: attacks, deaths, injuries, arrests, defects, deficits, scandals.
